newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul bank research body ups c/a deficit forecast.
newsitem.headline: Seoul bank research body ups c/a deficit forecast.

text.p: The Korea Institute of Finance said on Monday in a report that it had raised its forecast for the nation's current account deficit in calendar 1997 to $19 billion from its earlier forecast of a $16.7 billion shortfall.
The institute is a leading South Korean research body, established jointly by the nation's banks.
While the trade deficit is expected to narrow to $8.97 billion in 1997, deficits in the tourism industry and royalty payments will continue to expand, the report said.
South Korea posted a trade deficit of a provisional $20.38 billion in calendar 1996, up from $10.06 billion in 1995.
The central Bank of Korea has forecast this year's current account deficit at about $18 billion, compared with an estimated $22 billion deficit in 1996.
